ENSDELT312.text: This course examines sustainability through the lens of governance: “a process of rule-making and collective decision-making that includes both governmental and non-governmental actors in shaping public policy” (Fenger & Bekkers, 2016). Taking this lens, we ask questions such as how are sustainability policies on the local, national, and international level made and enforced? Which actors represent which interests, and which are most influential? How is public opinion on sustainability shaped, and how does public opinion shape politics? What, at the end of the day, determines effective policy for sustainability? By the end of this course, you will have gained a deep appreciation of the complexity of the governance dimension of sustainability, and have developed the theoretical and practical understanding to critically assess mainstream policy decisions.

audience.programmeDescription: VU Biology connects living systems from molecules and cells to organisms and ecosystems. It combines biochemistry, genetics, microbiology, physiology, evolution and ecology with laboratory and field methods, biological data analysis and a substantial individual research placement.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers three qualified study directions: living systems across biological levels; ecology and environmental health; and molecular biology, disease and neuroscience. Each contains substantial biological study with a different emphasis. The ecological option includes hands-on biological laboratory study alongside its environmental methods. Environmental technology and general data methods are specific complements, not replacements for specialist biological content. The VU microbiology sequence, assessed species-identification fieldwork and 24 EC research placement with integrated Science Skills remain important differences; optional UCR research does not automatically reproduce them.

curriculum.routeLabel: General Biology with five selected second-year options
curriculum.limitation: The Dutch 2026–2027 bachelor has 60 EC compulsory Year 1 study; 30 EC compulsory Year 2 study plus two separate 6 EC required choices and three 6 EC selected electives; then 30 EC open study, 6 EC Science Skills and a 24 EC thesis placement. The shown choices are Diversiteit van leven, Levensgemeenschappen, Global Change, Pathophysiology of Heart and Circulatory System, and Human Neurophysiology. Alternatives and repeated first-year lab/fieldwork options are not stacked. There is no formal graduation track. Science Skills requires passed Methodology and Research in Biology, Prediction and Analysis, and zero-credit Career Orientation 2. Career Orientation 1 is required for Orientation 2 and for the Methodology grade; both orientation courses must be completed before the final-year research. Thesis entry requires all 60 first-year EC and at least 42 second-year EC including Orientation 2, course registration, a VU supervisor and a placement approved and fully administered in OnStage. The placement spans 20 weeks, combining 16 full-time-equivalent research weeks with four Science Skills weeks. The first-day kick-off is compulsory. A Go/No Go review after 4–6 weeks considers the preliminary introduction, academic-writing participation and research attitude/quality. Final assessment covers research 40%, report 35%, oral presentation 20% and poster 5%; professional development must be satisfactory and every graded part at least 5.5. Science Skills requires a passed writing module and grades above 5.5 for statistics and communication, weighted 60/40; attendance and assignments require time alongside research. Lab safety, the Dutch diagnostic/refresher test and career orientation add no EC. The language requirement must be passed before the Biochemistry grade is awarded. BSA ordinarily requires 42 first-year EC, subject to exceptions. Practical/tutorial attendance follows unit manuals; listed diversity practicals/excursions and cardiovascular practicals/workgroups are compulsory, as are scheduled nonlecture Human Neurophysiology activities. Individual open choices need prior board approval, at least 12 EC at level 300 and at most 6 EC at level 100; eligible university/listed minors are exempt from prior approval. Foreign open study may include one 6 EC master unit that cannot be reused in a later master. Thesis and placement regulations apply. Optional minors do not create extra compulsory routes.
